page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.4xlarge is an extreme memory-optimized instance engineered for memory-intensive enterprise environments. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.5 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs. It incorporates 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an expansive 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 32.0 GB of RAM allocated per virtual core.

The compute subsystem is augmented by 24 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and vector extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI support. Benchmark performance exhibits strong memory subsystem throughput, scoring 2,782.31 on PassMark Memory and delivering 31.65 GB/s in single-threaded gzip compression. Compute benchmarks show solid baseline throughput, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,314.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 20,169.75, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 88.2 GB/s.

Architectural tradeoffs center around storage and compute density. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached Amazon EBS volumes for persistent storage, complemented by a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. Additionally, while the 4.5 GHz clock speed delivers capable per-thread performance, raw parallel compute is constrained by the 16-vCPU footprint, as highlighted by weak prompt processing on medium 7B language models at 27.64 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x2iezn.4xlarge is optimized for workloads where per-core software licensing costs are high but memory footprint requirements are extreme. The heavy RAM allocation minimizes licensing overhead per gigabyte of memory. This configuration is particularly suitable for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise electronic design automation (EDA), and heavy transactional relational databases.
